question: Should the existing public `openclawProgressKind` reply-payload seam be extended with permanent generic `tool-progress` semantics for Codex and channel plugins?
rationale: The structured-block defect is mechanical, but whether third-party plugins should depend on this new shared constant and predicate is a durable public API and ownership choice.

options.title: Extend the existing seam
options.body: Keep the generic kind public, document its producer and channel-consumer semantics, and land after the delivery repair and proof.

options.title: Keep the marker bundled-private
options.body: Use an internal bundled-runtime contract if generic tool progress is not intended as third-party plugin API.

options.title: Use preview infrastructure
options.body: Route these summaries through the established tool-progress preview pipeline if that is the canonical long-term owner.

recommendation.title: Extend the existing seam
recommendation.body: Keep the generic kind public, document its producer and channel-consumer semantics, and land after the delivery repair and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the exact public progress metadata seam being extended.
